title: MIT Builds a Memory Chip That Can Steer Current

editorial.topic: MIT magnetic-exchange superconducting memory and programmable diode
editorial.originality: WordPress recent posts, drafts, specific superconducting sandwich, cryogenic memory, Moodera, Ingla-Aynés searches; November GitHub archive checked. No duplicate located.
important_claims: Two ferromagnetic insulating layers sandwich an ultrathin superconducting film.
Selective single-cell switching demonstrated without disturbing neighboring cell.
Magnetically programmed nonvolatile memory only at cryogenic temperatures.
At lower temperature device provides preferred directional or resistive blocking modes.
Paper reports superconducting diode efficiency magnitude >60% at zero applied magnetic field, NOT 60% lower energy consumption.
No demonstrated dense commercial memory array or cooling-inclusive system power savings.

chart.reason: A numerical comparison chart would conflate diode nonreciprocity, power consumption and unrelated memory technologies; exact measured comparable dataset not released.
options_considered: Bar of energy savings: rejected, no tested system figures
Line chart of memory energy over time: rejected, no time series
Device state diagram: used authentic MIT research schematic rather than constructing a simplified diagram.
